text: package builds firm-level “high-growth firm” (HGF) / scale-indicators used OECD Scale project, produces disclosure-checked aggregate tables shared back OECD. behaviour-preserving translation OECD’s original Stata pipeline (MASTER_OECD_p2.5 worker .files) — see Analysis/stata.md Pseudocode/*.md package source repository full analysis translation built . Firm-level microdata confidential never leaves country whose national statistical institute holds , real data ships package. Every example uses small, fabricated data purely demonstrate interface — actual numbers meaningless.

title: Getting Started with OECDscaleup
text: Five pipeline functions, matching five original .files one--one: build_accounts_indicators() — cleans raw firm-level data constructs every derived indicator (growth rates, HGF flags, categories, multi-factor productivity, …). Every stage depends output. compute_characteristics() — descriptive statistics scaler populations. compute_persistence() — growth trajectories /scaling event (“transitions” “evolutions”). compute_contribution() — job/turnover creation-vs-destruction accounting. compute_predictors() — classifies scalers pre-period predictor quartile regresses scaling predictors. Stages 2-5 independent depend stage 1’s output. five pure functions — data frames , data frames — can tested used without touching filesystem. run_scaleup_pipeline() function performs file /O: reads raw .dta inputs, calls five functions order, writes every output CSV — mirroring MASTER_OECD_p2.’s role original package.

text: already data loaded R — instance ’re testing, piping data elsewhere R workflow — call five functions directly instead. ’s small synthetic example: compute_persistence() returns named list (transitions, evolutions_p1, evolutions_p2) since country’s panel may short produce three; compute_predictors() similarly returns list() entirely added_value, tangible_fixed_assets, labour_costs aren’t present input data. persistence elements — random 9-year panel doesn’t happen contain firm scales specifically within 2014-2016 window (transitions) panel reaching 2020 (evolutions), neither error. Real country panels spanning years, genuine scaling firms, populate one transitions, evolutions_p1, evolutions_p2.
code: set.seed(1) years <- 2010:2018 base_financials <- data.frame(   idf = rep(1:20, each = length(years)),   year = rep(years, times = 20),   sector_1d = "C",   sector_2d = 26,   sector_3d = 262,   region_2d = "FR10",   birth_year = 2000,   employment = as.vector(sapply(1:20, function(i) {     pmax(10, round(stats::rlnorm(1, log(30), 0.3) * (1 + stats::rnorm(1, 0.02, 0.1))^(seq_along(years) - 1)))   })),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) base_financials$turnover <- base_financials$employment * 100  cfg <- config_scaleup(   country = "FR",   input_dir = tempdir(), # unused by the pure functions themselves   output_dir = tempdir() )  accounts_indicators <- build_accounts_indicators(cfg, base_financials) characteristics <- compute_characteristics(cfg, accounts_indicators) head(characteristics) #> # A tibble: 6 × 19 #>    year sample category group       firm_count mean_employment_growth3y #>   <dbl> <chr>  <chr>    <chr>            <int>                    <dbl> #> 1  2013 HGE10  ALL      full sample          2                    0.509 #> 2  2014 HGE10  ALL      full sample          2                    0.501 #> 3  2015 HGE10  ALL      full sample          2                    0.517 #> 4  2016 HGE10  ALL      full sample          2                    0.390 #> 5  2017 HGE10  ALL      full sample          3                    0.456 #> 6  2018 HGE10  ALL      full sample          3                    0.456 #> # ℹ 13 more variables: mean_turnover_growth3y <dbl>, #> #   mean_employment_futgrowth <dbl>, mean_turnover_futgrowth <dbl>, #> #   share_acquisition <dbl>, L3share_young <dbl>, median_L3employment <dbl>, #> #   median_L3turnover <dbl>, median_employment <dbl>, median_turnover <dbl>, #> #   median_employment_growth3y <dbl>, median_turnover_growth3y <dbl>, #> #   median_employment_futgrowth <dbl>, median_turnover_futgrowth <dbl> persistence <- compute_persistence(cfg, accounts_indicators) names(persistence) #> NULL
